\bugonpage 4f7.3 replacement for lines $-10$ thru $-4$ (26.08.20)
Sometimes a $k$-ary relation is {\it{constant}}, meaning that it
is satisfied by only a single $k$-tuple. One interesting example is
the structure $S=(V,E,\{ab\})$, where $(V,E)$ is a graph with
special vertices $a$ and~$b$. Then a homomorphism $h$ from $S$ to the
relational structure $S'=(\{0,1\},{=},{\ne})$ will tell us that
$u\adj v$ implies $h(u)=h(v)$, and also that $h(a)\ne h(b)$.
Hence every vertex~$v$ {reachable} from~$a$ will have $h(v)=h(a)$,
and we can conclude that $b$ is unreachable. Conversely, if $a$ and~$b$
belong to different {components},
such a homomorphism can easily be found.\tighten
